note: Which committer identity owns which paths (plan.md 9). git records no session, so a seat declares itself: the committer is seat:<name> <name@seat.invalid> and the author stays the person. Read by check 6.
adopt: A session names its seat with `python bootstrap.py seat <role> --write` and commits with `python contracts/tools/seat_commit.py --seat <name> ...`, which sets the committer for that one commit. In a clone one seat uses alone, git config committer.name 'seat:<name>' and git config committer.email <name>@seat.invalid do the same for plain git commit (git has read these keys since 2.22); never where another seat is working, since the repository holds one value. One identity per session; two sessions sharing one identity is a hole the check cannot see.
names: <role>-<machine>-<YYYYMMDD>-<n>. Roles: design, meta, harness (from M5). Machines: office is the Office computer, macbook is the person's MacBook Air (given 2026-11-06); a new computer gets its tag from the person before its first seat. n counts within one role, machine and date. A name is never reissued.
addresses: seat.invalid is reserved by RFC 2606 and never routes; a seat identity is a label, not a mailbox.
path_syntax: an entry ending in / is a directory prefix; '*' alone means files at the repository root; anything else is one file. excludes are applied after paths.
self_registration: Standing rule of the person, 2026-11-09 (docs/ideas/20261109.md, plan.md 9): a session may add its own entry when the name follows the pattern on a machine tag already listed under names, the role is one of the three and is the one the person or the session's task names, paths and excludes are copied unchanged from an active seat of the same role, the entry lands in its own commit before any other work, and seated_by says self with the rule's date. A new role, a new machine tag or a wider path stays the person's. Check 6 enforces this (meta_agent/tasks/009 part 3): such a commit touches contracts/seats.json alone and adds one entry, and it is judged against the table as it was before the commit.
self_registration_from_note: The last commit before check 6 knew the rule (meta_agent/tasks/009 part 3). A commit at or before it that adds the committer's own entry is judged as it was then, by the boundary alone: 183c593 is this computer's design seat registering itself on the person's word of 2026-11-06, before there was a rule to follow.
concurrent: Several seats may share this working copy at the same time (the person, 2026-11-09). The repository-wide committer.name can hold one seat only, so with a second seat present the committer is set for the commit itself (GIT_COMMITTER_NAME, GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL) and the commit names its paths.
unknown_committer_note: A committer absent from this list is reported (PENDING), not refused, so that the person committing by hand is never blocked. --strict counts PENDING as failure.
enforced_from_note: The last commit before contracts/ existed (PLAN.ko.md v0.3.2, 2026-10-29). Check 6 reports rather than fails for commits at or before it; the four commits before it are the plan alone, all by the design seat.
machines_note: A tag is given by the person before a computer's first seat. `git config meta-agent.machine <tag>` records it in a clone so that `python bootstrap.py seat <role>` can read it. A new computer's tag is added here by a seat that already exists, citing the person's words, before the new computer's first session seats itself: a self-registration may change nothing but its own entry.

harness.note: from M5 (plan.md 9); until a harness seat exists the meta seat writes meta_agent/harness/

roles_note: What every active seat of a role owns; an entry's paths, excludes and owns equal its role's row (check 6). A wider path or a new role is the person's. 2026-11-09 (meta_agent/tasks/009): the design row gains .github/ for the gate's workflow, which the person permitted, and meta_agent/inbox/seats/ for notes between seats; the harness row is written down from plan.md 9 with the claims and notes folders every role may write.

seats.note: Root files, contracts/, docs/, the agent's instructions and settings, and the meta_agent/ skeleton M0 creates (tasks, templates, eval, the empty logs, the inbox's README, LINKS.md and drop/.gitkeep). It does not write cards, requests, profiles, knowledge, cases, harness records or builds.
